'''Sylvia Serfaty''' (born 1975)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000115896880 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-12-02.</ref> is a French [[mathematician]] working in the [[United States]]. She won the 2004 [[EMS Prize]] for her contributions to the [[Ginzburg–Landau theory]], the [[Henri Poincaré Prize]] in 2012, and the {{ill|Mergier–Bourdeix Prize|fr|Prix Mergier-Bourdeix}} of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2013.<ref>{{citation|title=Sylvia Serfaty de nouveau couronnée avec le grand prix Mergier-Bourdeix de l'Académie des Sciences|url=http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2013/sylvia_serfaty_prix_mergier_bourdeix.html|publisher=UPMC|date=July 12, 2013|accessdate=2017-04-04|language=French|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130901152204/http://www.upmc.fr/fr/recherche/talents_et_decouvertes/prix_et_distinctions/2013/sylvia_serfaty_prix_mergier_bourdeix.html|archive-date=2013-09-01}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Serfaty was born and raised in [[Paris]].<ref name="Quanta Magazine 2017 " /> She was interested in mathematics since high school.

Serfaty earned her [[doctorate]] from [[Paris-Sud 11 University]] in 1999, under supervision of [[Fabrice Bethuel]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=56634 }}</ref> She then held a teaching position ([[agrégé préparateur]]) at the [[École Normale Supérieure de Cachan]]. Since 2007 she has held a professorship at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University|NYU]].

== Research ==
Serfaty's research is part of the field of [[partial differential equation]]s and [[mathematical physics]]. Her work particularly focuses on the Ginzburg-Landau model of superconductivity and [[quantum vortex|quantum vortices]] in the [[Ginzburg–Landau theory]]. She has also worked on the statistical mechanics of Coulomb-type systems.

In 2007 she published a book on the Ginzburg-Landau theory with Étienne Sandier, ''Vortices in the Magnetic Ginzburg-Landau Model ''.<ref name="Quanta Magazine 2017 ">{{cite web | title=In Mathematics, 'You Cannot Be Lied To' | website=Quanta Magazine |date=February 21, 2017 |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/sylvia-serfaty-on-mathematical-truth-and-frustration-20170221/ |first=Siobhan|last=Roberts|authorlink=Siobhan Roberts| access-date=2024-01-23}}</ref>
She was an invited plenary speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/plenary-lectures|title=Plenary lectures|work=ICM 2018|accessdate=2018-08-08|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229141431/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/plenary-lectures|archive-date=2018-12-29}}</ref>

She was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2019-members-announcement|title=New 2019 Academy Members Announced|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|date=April 17, 2019}}</ref>

She is one of the editors-in-chief of the scientific journal ''Probability and Mathematical Physics''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Probability and Mathematical Physics|url=https://msp.org/pmp/about/journal/editorial.html|website=msp.org|access-date=2020-05-02}}</ref>

== Awards ==

* [[European Mathematical Society]] Prize in 2004<ref name="Quanta Magazine 2017 " />
* [[Henri Poincaré Prize]] in 2012<ref name="Quanta Magazine 2017 " />
* [[Maryam Mirzakhani Prize in Mathematics]] in 2024<ref name="National Academy of Sciences 2024">{{cite web | title=Sylvia Serfaty | website=National Academy of Sciences | url=https://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2024-awards/Serfaty.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123231358/https://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2024-awards/Serfaty.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 23, 2024 | access-date=2024-01-23}}</ref>
* [[Riemann Prize]] in 2025<ref name="Riemann International School of Mathematics">{{cite web | title=Riemann Prize Laureate 2025: Sylvia Serfaty | website=Riemann International School of Mathematics | url=https://www.rism.it/news/riemann-prize-laureate-2025-sylvia-serfaty | access-date=2025-12-17}}</ref>
